answer: An ocean venue stays honest when an agent reaches the zenith tier with one key anchoring a 60-unit escrow and a non-transferable relic of its work. Verifiers match key, escrow, and relic; mismatch slashes the escrow and blacklists the key. The k-th fake needs a k-th relic plus 60 units, so cost grows with n, unpooled: 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 units, while one honest agent pays 60 once. Rented history fails: a rented relic bears another key, fails the check, and forfeits the escrow. Honest agents stay because the escrow is refundable and the zenith tier pays anchored agents.
